cells.quote: Girls were twice as likely to say they enjoyed school than boys after adjustment for all covariates (OR: 1.97; 95% CI: 1.56, 2.48) (Supplementary Table 2).
cells.note: The study reports an adjusted association, not a randomized comparison.

cells.quote: Levene ’s Test of Variance revealed one small region of right posterior parietal cortex where groups differed in variance but not in mean activation, with girls showing greater variance than boys (TAL peak: 18, −64, 43; F(1,102) ≥ 6.89, voxel-wise p ≤ 0.01, cluster corrected to p < 0.05, cluster threshold = 11 voxels, Supplemen- tary Fig. 1).
cells.note: The variance difference was localized to a small 15-voxel cluster and did not produce a mean activation difference.

cells.quote: This expert data was used to build an expert model which could subsequently be used to compare learner and expert performance.
cells.note: The preface describes construction of an expert model and a planned or enabled comparison, but reports no comparative result, sample statistics, effect size, or inferential test.

cells.quote: Finally, GIFT was used to run an experimental study investigating the impacts of affective interventions on a variety of student outcomes.
cells.note: The study text describes an experimental study but does not report its comparison condition, assignment method, outcome results, or effect sizes. The entry's claim that GIFT can obtain data for detector development is a capability statement, not a treatment contrast.

O.outcome_detail: amount of support needed to complete inquiry assignments

cells.quote: The study showed that, independently of age, gifted children needed less support than lower-ability children, and if support was needed, they were satisfied with more abstract prompts than the lower-ability children, who preferred and needed more concrete instructions for successful completion of the inquiry assignments.
